drafts.walkScript: Start with clock and time. A clock measures time. In the same way, a thermometer measures temperature. A doctor uses a thermometer, and hour belongs with clocks.
Look at author and novel. An author writes a novel. A composer writes a symphony, so symphony fits. A piano is played, and a note is only part of a symphony.
Start with shepherd and sheep. A shepherd looks after sheep. A cowboy looks after cattle in the same way. Horns are part of cattle, and wool comes from sheep.
Look at library and books. A library holds books. A gallery holds paintings in the same way. A brush makes a painting, and a frame is only part of one.
Start with drought and rain. A drought is a long time without enough rain. A famine is a long time without enough food. Hunger is what a famine causes, and cloud belongs with rain.
Look at captain and crew. A captain leads a crew. A conductor leads an orchestra, so orchestra fits. Ship goes with the captain, and a violin is only part of an orchestra.
Start with recipe and meal. A recipe is the plan for making a meal. A blueprint is the plan for making a building. A brick is only part of a building, and kitchen goes with meals.
Look at chapter and novel. A chapter is one part of a novel. A scene is one part of a play. A ticket goes with plays. A line is part of a scene, which is the wrong way round.
Start with warm and scorching. Scorching is far hotter than warm. In the same way, soaked is far wetter than damp. Wet is only a little wetter, and sunny belongs with warm weather.
Look at breeze and gale. A gale is a very strong breeze. A downpour is a very heavy shower. Drizzle is lighter than a shower, the wrong way round. A kite goes with wind.
Start with whisper and shout. A shout is a much stronger use of the voice than a whisper. A stare is a much stronger look than a glance. Look is just the plain word, and loud belongs with shout.
Look at whisper and scream. A scream is a much louder sound than a whisper. A wail is a much louder cry than a whimper. Cry is just the plain word, and tears go with crying.
Start with annoyed and furious. Furious is a much stronger kind of annoyed. Delighted is a much stronger kind of pleased. Happy is about the same as pleased, and angry belongs with the first pair.
Look at wheat and flour. Wheat is ground to make flour. In the same way, grapes are squeezed to make juice. Bread is a step further on, and grapes grow on a vine.
Start with sculptor and marble. A sculptor shapes marble to make art. A potter shapes clay in the same way. A vase is what a potter makes, and a statue is what a sculptor makes.
Look at herd and cattle. A herd is a group of cattle. A flock is a group of sheep. A cow is one animal in a herd, and wool comes from sheep.
Start with novel and chapter. A novel is made up of chapters. A poem is made up of verses, so verse fits. A book holds poems, which is the wrong way round. An author is the writer, not a part.
Look at dictionary and word. A dictionary is a book full of words. An atlas is a book full of maps. A library holds atlases, the wrong way round, and geography is just the subject.
Start with cowardice and bravery. They are opposites. Cruelty and kindness are opposites too, so kindness fits. Violence goes with cruelty, and fear goes with cowardice.
Look at witness and trial. A witness is a person who takes part in a trial. A referee is a person who takes part in a match. A judge belongs with a trial, and a goal is scored in a match.
Start with drop and ocean. A drop is a tiny bit of an ocean. A grain of sand is a tiny bit of a desert. A camel lives in a desert, and a wave belongs with the ocean.
Look at sketch and painting. A sketch is a rough first try before a painting. A draft is a rough first try before an essay. An outline comes before a draft, the wrong way round. A pen is just a tool.
Start with forget and remember. They are opposites. Doubt and believe are opposites too, so believe fits. Memory goes with remember, and worry is close to doubt.

Look at apprentice and master. An apprentice is a learner who grows into a master. A sapling is a young tree that can grow into an oak. An acorn comes before a sapling, the wrong way round. A branch is only part of a tree.
